easy.explanation: The LORD commanded Jonah to arise and go to Nineveh.
easy.q: Where did the LORD command Jonah to go?

easy.explanation: The LORD said, “cry against it,” because of its wickedness.
easy.q: What was Jonah to do in Nineveh?

easy.explanation: Jonah rose up to flee unto Tarshish from the presence of the LORD.

answers: To find a ship to Tarshish
To meet the people of Nineveh
medium.explanation: Jonah went to Joppa and found a ship going to Tarshish.
medium.q: Why did Jonah go down to Joppa?

medium.explanation: Jonah paid the fare thereof, meaning the cost of the passage.
medium.q: What does “the fare thereof” refer to?

answers: He hurried to obey the LORD
He tried to escape his mission
He sought to reach Nineveh by sea
medium.explanation: Instead of going to Nineveh, Jonah went to Joppa and boarded a ship for Tarshish.
medium.q: What does Jonah’s sequence of actions show?

answers: The LORD sent him to Nineveh, but Jonah went toward Tarshish
The LORD told him to sail, but Jonah stayed on land
The LORD told him to be silent, but Jonah cried aloud
challenge.explanation: The LORD commanded Jonah to go to Nineveh, but Jonah fled toward Tarshish.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between the LORD’s command and Jonah’s action?

challenge.explanation: The phrase “from the presence of the LORD” is repeated in the description of Jonah’s flight.
challenge.q: Which phrase emphasizes that Jonah tried to escape God’s command?

answers: He was practically preparing to travel to Tarshish
He was paying for a sacrifice
He had received a new commission
challenge.explanation: Jonah paid the fare and went down into the ship to travel to Tarshish.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Jonah paying the fare?

easy.explanation: The LORD sent out a great wind into the sea.
easy.q: What did the LORD send into the sea?

easy.explanation: They cast forth the wares that were in the ship to lighten it.
easy.q: What did the mariners cast into the sea?

easy.explanation: Jonah went down into the sides of the ship and was fast asleep.
easy.q: What was Jonah doing while the mariners struggled?

answers: Because the ship was like to be broken
Because they wanted to reach Nineveh
medium.explanation: The mighty tempest made the ship seem likely to break apart.
medium.q: Why did the mariners cry every man unto his god?

answers: The highest parts of the ship
The inner or lower parts of the ship
The cargo carried by the ship
medium.explanation: Jonah went down into the inner or lower part of the ship and slept there.
medium.q: What does “the sides of the ship” mean in this passage?

answers: The mariners struggled while Jonah slept
The mariners slept while Jonah cast out the wares
The mariners fled while Jonah repaired the ship
medium.explanation: The mariners worked urgently, while Jonah lay fast asleep.
medium.q: What contrast appears between the mariners and Jonah?

answers: Jonah was sleeping despite the great danger
Jonah was in charge of the mariners
challenge.explanation: The shipmaster had to wake Jonah because he was sleeping during the dangerous storm.
challenge.q: What does the shipmaster waking Jonah emphasize?

answers: The wind and tempest caused the mariners to struggle and cast out wares
Jonah’s sleep caused the ship to reach Nineveh
The mariners’ prayers caused Jonah to come on deck
challenge.explanation: Because of the storm, the mariners struggled and threw cargo into the sea.

answers: Arise and call upon his God
challenge.explanation: The shipmaster said, “arise, call upon thy God.”
challenge.q: What did the shipmaster ask Jonah to do?

easy.explanation: They cast lots to know for whose cause the evil was upon them.
easy.q: What did the mariners do to discover whose fault caused the trouble?
Upon whom did the lot fall?
What people did Jonah say he belonged to?

answers: What shall we do unto thee, that the sea may be calm?
medium.explanation: They asked what they should do so that the sea might be calm unto them.
medium.q: What did the mariners ask Jonah after the lot fell upon him?

medium.explanation: They asked Jonah what his occupation, or work, was.
medium.q: What does “occupation” mean in the mariners’ question?

answers: Jonah said he fled from the presence of the LORD
Jonah said he did not know the sea
Jonah asked them to sail to Tarshish
medium.explanation: They knew Jonah was fleeing from the LORD, and this greatly frightened them.
medium.q: Why were the men exceedingly afraid?

answers: Jonah acknowledged God’s rule over all creation while trying to flee from Him
Jonah claimed that God ruled only the dry land
Jonah said the sea and land belonged to the mariners
challenge.explanation: Jonah confessed that the LORD made both sea and land, even though he had tried to flee from Him.
challenge.q: What tension appears in Jonah’s statement that the LORD made “the sea and the dry land”?

answers: They were trying to understand who he was and what caused the trouble
They wanted to make Jonah captain
challenge.explanation: They questioned his occupation, origin, country, and people to understand the cause of the evil.
challenge.q: What can be understood from the many questions the mariners asked Jonah?

answers: The lot identified Jonah, and they questioned him about his situation
The lot identified the sea, and they abandoned the ship
The lot identified Nineveh, and they sailed there
challenge.explanation: After the lot fell on Jonah, the mariners asked him who he was and what he had done.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the casting of lots and the mariners’ response?

paragraphs.title: Jonah Is Thrown into the Sea

easy.explanation: Jonah said, “Take me up, and cast me forth into the sea.”
easy.q: What did Jonah suggest would calm the sea?

easy.explanation: The men rowed hard to bring the ship to the land.
easy.q: What did the mariners try to do before casting Jonah into the sea?

easy.explanation: After Jonah was cast into the sea, the sea ceased from her raging.
easy.q: What happened after Jonah was cast into the sea?

answers: Because it was for his sake
Because they had not rowed hard enough
Because they did not know the way to Tarshish
medium.explanation: Jonah said, “for my sake this great tempest is upon you.”
medium.q: Why did Jonah say the storm was upon the mariners?

answers: The blood of a person who is not guilty
The blood of one of the mariners
medium.explanation: The mariners asked the LORD not to charge them with the death of an innocent person.
medium.q: What does “innocent blood” mean in this passage?

answers: The sea continued to be tempestuous against them
They had lost all the ship’s wares
medium.explanation: They could not reach land because the sea continued to rage against them.
medium.q: Why could the mariners not bring the ship back to land?

answers: They tried to avoid guilt for innocent blood and appealed to the LORD
They had no concern for Jonah’s life
They wanted Jonah to lead them
challenge.explanation: They cried unto the LORD and asked not to perish or be charged with innocent blood.
challenge.q: What does the mariners’ prayer before casting Jonah overboard show?

answers: The mariners tried to reach land, prayed, cast Jonah into the sea, and the sea became calm
They cast Jonah into the sea, prayed, and then tried to reach land
They prayed, reached land, and then cast Jonah into the sea
challenge.explanation: This is the order described in verses 13–15.
challenge.q: What is the correct sequence of events?

answers: Jonah admitted the storm was for his sake, and after he was cast out the sea became calm
Jonah denied responsibility, and the sea became calm
Jonah prayed, and the sea became calm without any further action
challenge.explanation: Jonah identified himself as the cause of the storm, and the sea ceased raging after he was cast out.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between Jonah’s confession and the calming of the sea?

easy.explanation: The men feared the LORD exceedingly.
easy.q: Whom did the mariners greatly fear after the sea became calm?

easy.explanation: They offered a sacrifice unto the LORD.
easy.q: What did the mariners offer unto the LORD?

easy.explanation: The verse says that they made vows.
easy.q: What else did the mariners do?

answers: Jonah being cast into the sea
The wares being cast overboard alone
medium.explanation: After Jonah was cast into the sea, the sea ceased from her raging.
medium.q: What caused the change in the sea?

medium.explanation: The mariners made vows, meaning promises or solemn commitments.
medium.q: What does “vows” mean in this verse?

answers: They feared the LORD, offered a sacrifice, and made vows
They went back to sleep below deck
medium.explanation: Their response was fear of the LORD, sacrifice, and vows.
medium.q: What did the mariners do after the sea became calm?

answers: They moved from crying to their own gods to greatly fearing the LORD
They moved from great fear to ignoring the LORD
They moved from praying to the LORD to fleeing from Him
challenge.explanation: At first they cried to their own gods, but afterward they feared the LORD exceedingly.
challenge.q: What major change occurred in the mariners’ attitude toward God?

answers: The mariners saw the calm as the LORD’s act and responded with reverence and gratitude
They thought the sea became calm entirely by itself
They did not connect the events
challenge.explanation: After the sea ceased raging, they feared the LORD, offered a sacrifice, and made vows.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the connection between the calm sea, sacrifice, and vows?

answers: “They feared the LORD exceedingly” and performed acts of worship
They cast the wares into the sea
Jonah slept in the sides of the ship
challenge.explanation: The phrase “feared the LORD exceedingly,” together with the sacrifice and vows, emphasizes their strong response.
challenge.q: Which detail emphasizes the strength of the mariners’ response?
